Region parsed from endpoint hostname pattern s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com (fallback us-west-004). Signing key chain: HMAC(k="AWS4"+secret, date) > region > "s3" > "aws4_request", then HMAC of the canonical request. Use globalThis.crypto.subtle only (Workers compatible). Perform the fetch with the global fetch. photo_url = {B2_ENDPOINT}/{B2_BUCKET}/{key}.
Tests use a STUBBED fetch (inject via a module-level setter or options callback) capturing the Request; do NOT hit the network. Assert: (1) missing creds throws B2ConfigError; (2) method PUT and URL equal endpoint/bucket/test-key; (3) SignedHeaders string is exactly content-type;host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date; (4) with fixed opts.now, the Credential date segment and x-amz-date are deterministic; (5) signing twice with identical inputs yields identical signatures (determinism); (6) changing one body byte changes x-amz-content-sha256; (7) signature is 64 lowercase hex chars.
WORK RED-FIRST: tests first, watch them fail, then implement.
VERIFY: pnpm exec vitest run test/b2.test.ts exits 0.

final_response:
Done. `pnpm exec vitest run test/b2.test.ts` is green (8/8) and `pnpm typecheck` passes.

**Delivered (only the two in-scope files):**
- `src/storage/b2.ts` — exports `B2ConfigError extends Error` and `uploadPhoto(env, key, body, contentType, opts?)`. Missing/empty `B2_KEY_ID`/`B2_APP_KEY` throws `B2ConfigError`; otherwise it computes the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the body via WebCrypto, builds the SigV4 canonical request (`SignedHeaders=content-type;host;x-amz-content-sha256;x-amz-date`), derives the signing key through the full HMAC chain (`AWS4<secret>` → date → region → `s3` → `aws4_request`), and PUTs to `{B2_ENDPOINT}/{B2_BUCKET}/{key}`. Region is parsed from `s3.<region>.backblazeb2.com` with fallback `us-west-004`; `x-amz-date` comes from `opts.now ?? new Date()`. Fetch goes through a module-level indirection with `setB2Fetch()` for injection; all crypto uses `crypto.subtle` only.
- `test/b2.test.ts` — written first, confirmed failing before implementation. Covers all seven required assertions plus `photo_url` shape, using a stubbed fetch that captures the constructed `Request`; no network access.

One note: `@cloudflare/workers-types` declares `crypto` as a global const rather than on `globalThis`, so the code references bare `crypto.subtle` — identical runtime object in Workers and Node. No git commit made, per instructions.
